text:
sara: FYI customer 'AcmeMaps' escalated — dedicated pool q3-prod kept hitting 429s for ~7m. They report UI queueing and big spikes that didn't produce capacity fast enough. Request from support to triage ASAP.

dan: @sara can you paste the customer request IDs / example timestamps? which model and route?

sara: route: /v1/generate (gpt-neo-xl-quant), timestamps start 2026-05-02T14:05Z. sample request IDs: req_8f3a, req_8f3b. Payloads are typical 512 tokens. They saw ~20 rps burst.

mike: grabbing autoscaler logs now. quick note — pool q3-prod has min_replicas=2, max_replicas=12, scale_up_cooldown=60s, scale_increment=1. If burst > capacity we usually add 1 replica/min unless we hit node provisioning delays.

irene: customer supplied their own VPC nodes? or using Redwood-managed nodepool?

sara: Redwood-managed nodepool. No nodepool changes on their side.

mike: pasting relevant autoscaler snippet:```
[2026-05-02T14:06:01Z] autoscaler INFO desired_replicas=8 current_replicas=2 reason=policy:queued_requests(140)>threshold
[2026-05-02T14:07:02Z] autoscaler INFO scaling: current=2 -> desired=3 provision_request_id=prov-492
[2026-05-02T14:08:05Z] autoscaler WARN node-provision-delay reason=insufficient-capacity cloud_status=delayed
[2026-05-02T14:09:02Z] autoscaler INFO scaling: current=3 -> desired=4 provision_request_id=prov-493
[2026-05-02T14:11:12Z] autoscaler INFO scaling complete current=6 desired=8
```

dan: looks like provision latency is the issue — provisioning stuck for ~2–3m. Any node errors from kube?

mike: kube shows a repeating taint/evict cycle on nodepool nodes:```
May 02 14:06:40 node-rc-12 kubelet[...]: Eviction threshold reached: node memory pressure
May 02 14:06:45 kube-controller: cordon node-rc-12: OOM from gpu-driver processes
May 02 14:07:10 cloud-provisioner: launch vm request accepted -> pending network-attach
May 02 14:08:30 cloud-provisioner: vm booted but image-pull slow -> kubelet NotReady until 14:10
```

irene: noisy neighbor / GPU OOMs on existing nodes could reduce effective capacity so autoscaler kept requesting more but physical nodes weren't usable. Any recent image changes or heavy batched jobs?

sara: customer says they had a heavy internal batch ingestion job ~14:04 that we saw as sudden GPU memory jumps on two nodes.

jules: I see repeated 503s in the support logs while autoscaler was still provisioning. Customers see retries -> billing churn risk.

mike: immediate mitigation options: increase min_replicas to 4 for q3-prod (gives headroom), temporarily enable burst_capacity (allows queue spilling to warm standby), or evict noisy pods. I can manually bump min_replicas now if ops agree.

dan: we should also confirm scheduler quotas with cloud provider — slow network image pulls are a recurring flake in region-us-west2. If we bump min_replicas we may still hit provisioning queue but fewer scale steps required.

irene: propose runbook: 1) set min_replicas=4, 2) enable burst_capacity (30s) for 15m window, 3) cordon/evict node-rc-12 and drain noisy pods, 4) follow up incident postmortem with provider.

sara: customer requested ETA for fix. Can we do the bump now?

mike: I'll apply min_replicas=4 and enable burst now. Pushing change.```kubectl patch dedicatedpool q3-prod -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":4}}'```

autoscale-bot: change accepted: min_replicas from 2 -> 4 (applied by mike) at 2026-05-02T14:12:03Z.

mike: burst enabled (burst_window=30s) and started draining node-rc-12. Watching metrics.

jules: support updated customer at 14:14:10 — they see reduced queueing and fewer 429s. Still a few 503s as nodes finish boot.

sara: customer confirmed degraded but improving at 14:16Z. They asked for permanent recommendations to avoid recurrence.

dan: long-term fixes: increase steady min_replicas for this pool (based on 99th traffic), add image caching on nodes to avoid slow pulls, and add a cold-warm node strategy (keep a small pool of warm nodes with cached images). Also consider faster node types or node reuse for burst.

irene: file a follow-up ticket with infra + provider for investigation of image-pull slowness and OOMs. Assign to @mike and @dan.

mike: created infra ticket INF-2019 and linked customer case. Will run a repro with synthetic 25 rps 512 token payloads to validate autoscaler behavior under warm vs cold starts.

sara: thanks team. I'll keep customer updated and close the support escalation once metrics are stable for 30m. :thumbsup:

jules: quick note — billing flagged some retry inflation. We should flag refunds if customer incurred significant extra tokens due to retries.

dan: good call — finance/sales to review case. I will add to postmortem.

autoscale-bot: incident-severity=minor owner=mike status=mitigated window=2026-05-02T14:05Z-2026-05-02T14:16Z

sara: closing loop in 30m unless new regressions. Thanks all.
